A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we developed a self-supervised Siamese learning framework for depth estimation on stereo images, and validated it on robotic partial nephrectomies, where the results showed that the proposed framework can estimate depth maps for surgical scenes, and the estimated depth maps are accurate enough to be used for AR.
we propose a novel self-supervised learning method for depth estimation in the surgical setting using stereo image pairs.
we propose a deep-learning-based framework for surgical scene stereo matching, which is able to estimate the depth of the surgical scene without ground truth data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
self-supervised depth estimation using stereo image pairs is a promising alternative to ground-truth depth annotation, and can provide accurate depth predictions in robotic surgery.
self-supervision can be used to train deep networks on stereo image pairs for surgical scene depth, and that this can be applied to other surgical procedures and robotic platforms.
self-supervision enables scalable data acquisition for depth estimation.
